story_type: first crewed orbital rendezvous: two capsules one foot apart, back to back launches from one pad, historic color film
hook: Two spacecraft, one foot apart, 185 miles up.
narration: These two spacecraft flew within one foot of each other, a hundred and eighty five miles above the Pacific.
It was December 1965. Gemini 7 had launched first, with Frank Borman and Jim Lovell, for fourteen days in orbit.
Launch crews moved a second Titan rocket onto the same pad and worked around the clock to get Gemini 6 ready.
On December fifteenth, after a frustrating delay, Gemini 6 finally roared away to chase them.
To catch another spacecraft, you have to match its orbit and its speed, about seventeen thousand miles an hour.
outcome: Gemini 6 closed to within one foot of Gemini 7, a space age first on the road to the Moon.
title: Two spacecraft one foot apart, 1965
question_comment: Could you hold a spacecraft one foot from another at seventeen thousand miles an hour?
